decisions.reason: As a newly launched sensor module that extends the core modular sensing platform, its market potential is still being learned and the option value of keeping it available likely exceeds its near-term carrying cost.
Because it is explicitly the new generation replacing an older voltage measurement module, it fits the established product line closely and is very unlikely to be withdrawn so soon after launch.
The MQTT proxy is a low-cost software complement to the hardware ecosystem, so management would typically keep this option open while adoption across industrial and IoT use cases develops.

A CAN bus interface is strategically relevant for German automation and embedded customers, and despite some uncertainty about demand the product strengthens the platform with manageable continuation costs.

The CO2 sensor module is somewhat more niche and may face demand and component uncertainty, but as a recent environmental sensing launch it still has enough unresolved upside to justify staying on the market.

The touch panel accessory appears less central than core modules and could be dropped if uptake is weak, yet after only a short time on the market management would likely continue observing demand rather than exit immediately.
